rule: **Parameterless members are typed receivers (decision A)**: a receiver that is a call of a parameterless method, a `def` without a parameter list, a property getter, or an abstract member, with a declared type (Scala `def metadata: Map[..]`, `analysis.metadata.insert(..)`), names that type: `Map#insert` — left as a `metadata.insert` low guess it is wrong. | Typed receivers (decision A, all statically typed languages and typed PHP/Groovy declarations): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), enum-variant/data construction (Rust `Some(x)`, `E::V(..)`, Haskell `Con {..}`), casts, language constructs (`isset`, `empty`, `sizeof`), declarations/function heads, module attributes, typespecs, field access without a call.
notes: `this.store` is a property getter declared `: Db`, so `this.store.save(...)` names `app.Db#save` (not `store.save`, low). `this.config()` is a call of a parameterless method declared `: Config`, so `.load()` on it names `app.Config#load` (not `.load`, low). Reading the getter `this.store` is field access without a written call: no edge to `App#store`.
